questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Occupational health & industrial diseases
questions.stem: Pneumoconiosis is best defined as:
options: Accumulation of dust in the lungs with tissue reaction to its presence
questions.concept: Silicosis, coal worker's pneumoconiosis, asbestosis, byssinosis and bagassosis are the important forms. They are notifiable and compensable occupational diseases in India.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Occupational health & industrial diseases
questions.stem: Byssinosis, caused by cotton dust, is characterised by:
options: Chest tightness and dyspnoea worst on the first day back at work (Monday fever)
questions.concept: The improvement over the working week with recurrence after a break is the diagnostic clue. Radiographs are typically normal, unlike the fibrotic pneumoconioses.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Occupational health & industrial diseases
questions.stem: The most important measure to prevent occupational disease is:
options: Engineering control at source such as enclosure, ventilation and substitution
questions.concept: The hierarchy of control places elimination and substitution first, then engineering and administrative controls, with personal protective equipment last because it depends on individual compliance.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Occupational health & industrial diseases
questions.stem: Under the Factories Act, a notifiable occupational disease must be reported by:
options: The factory medical officer or medical practitioner to the Chief Inspector of Factories
questions.concept: The Act also regulates working hours, welfare facilities, hazardous processes and the appointment of safety officers, and mandates periodic medical examination for workers in hazardous processes.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Occupational health & industrial diseases
questions.stem: Chronic lead poisoning in an industrial worker is best monitored by:
options: Blood lead level, with blood ALA and zinc protoporphyrin as supporting tests
questions.concept: Features include anaemia with basophilic stippling, a gum lead line, wrist drop from radial nerve palsy, abdominal colic and, in children, encephalopathy with lasting cognitive impairment.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Occupational health & industrial diseases
questions.stem: Occupational noise-induced hearing loss characteristically shows:
options: A 4000 Hz dip on audiometry, bilateral and sensorineural
questions.concept: It is entirely preventable by engineering control and hearing protection but irreversible once established. Permissible exposure is 90 dB for 8 hours, halving the duration for each 5 dB increase.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Occupational health & industrial diseases
questions.stem: Caisson disease in compressed air workers is prevented by:
questions.concept: Nitrogen bubbles form on rapid decompression causing the bends, chokes and staggers, with chronic dysbaric osteonecrosis. Recompression in a hyperbaric chamber treats acute cases.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Occupational health & industrial diseases
questions.stem: The Employees State Insurance Act provides:
options: Medical care and cash benefits to insured workers and their dependants
questions.concept: ESI covers sickness, maternity, disablement, dependants and funeral benefits, funded by employer and employee contributions - a contributory social insurance model for organised sector workers.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Occupational health & industrial diseases
questions.stem: Sick building syndrome is characterised by:
options: Non-specific symptoms relieved on leaving the building, without a single identifiable cause
questions.concept: Headache, eye and throat irritation, fatigue and poor concentration relate to inadequate ventilation and indoor pollutants. Building-related illness, by contrast, has a specific identifiable cause such as legionellosis.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Occupational health & industrial diseases
questions.stem: Pre-placement examination in occupational health serves to:
options: Match the worker to a job they can safely perform and establish a baseline record
questions.concept: It is a placement rather than a rejection exercise, and the baseline is essential for later attributing any change to occupational exposure in medico-legal and compensation proceedings.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Environmental health: air, noise, housing, climate
questions.stem: The indicator organism of faecal contamination of water is:
questions.concept: E. coli is chosen because it is always present in faeces, survives slightly longer than most pathogens and is easily detected. Any coliform in treated piped water indicates unsatisfactory quality.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Environmental health: air, noise, housing, climate
questions.stem: The most effective single method of purifying water at household level is:
questions.concept: Boiling kills all pathogens including cysts and viruses but does not remove chemical contaminants and offers no residual protection against recontamination, which chlorination provides.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Environmental health: air, noise, housing, climate
questions.stem: The recommended residual free chlorine in drinking water after contact time is:
options: 0.5 mg per litre after one hour contact
questions.concept: The orthotolidine test measures residual chlorine. Break-point chlorination ensures the demand is satisfied first, and the residual guards against recontamination in the distribution system.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Environmental health: air, noise, housing, climate
questions.stem: The commonest indoor air pollutant causing respiratory disease among rural Indian women is:
questions.concept: Biomass smoke causes COPD, acute respiratory infection in children, low birth weight and cataract. The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana promoting LPG addresses this directly.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Environmental health: air, noise, housing, climate
questions.stem: The air pollutant most closely associated with cardiorespiratory mortality is:
options: PM2.5, fine particulate matter penetrating to the alveoli
questions.concept: Particles under 2.5 micrometres reach the alveoli and enter the circulation, causing systemic inflammation. India's National Clean Air Programme targets reduction in PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Environmental health: air, noise, housing, climate
questions.stem: Optimal housing standards recommend that a living room should have a floor area of at least:
options: Nine to eleven square metres per person
questions.concept: Overcrowding is defined by persons per room and floor space and facilitates transmission of tuberculosis, measles and respiratory infection - which is why housing is a determinant of health.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Environmental health: air, noise, housing, climate
questions.stem: Noise above what intensity causes hearing damage on prolonged exposure?
questions.concept: Permissible exposure is 90 dB for 8 hours in India, with duration halved for each 5 dB rise. Noise also causes annoyance, sleep disturbance, hypertension and impaired task performance.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Environmental health: air, noise, housing, climate
questions.stem: The greenhouse effect and climate change affect health chiefly through:
options: Heat stress, changing vector distribution, extreme weather and food and water insecurity
questions.concept: Warming extends the range and season of Aedes and Anopheles mosquitoes, altering dengue and malaria distribution, while heat waves cause direct mortality in the elderly and outdoor workers.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Environmental health: air, noise, housing, climate
questions.stem: Arsenic contamination of groundwater in West Bengal causes:
options: Hyperkeratosis, raindrop pigmentation and skin, bladder and lung cancer
questions.concept: The permissible limit is 0.01 mg/L. Chronic arsenicosis also causes peripheral vascular disease with blackfoot disease and Mees lines on the nails; mitigation requires alternative water sources.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Environmental health: air, noise, housing, climate
questions.stem: The sanitation barrier in preventing faeco-oral disease works by:
options: Interrupting transmission from faeces to the new host through the five Fs
questions.concept: Fingers, flies, fields, fluids and food are the routes. Safe excreta disposal and hand hygiene break the chain, which is why the Swachh Bharat Mission targets open defecation free status.
